text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Credit Lyonnais chairman Jean Peyrelevade has written to Finance Minister Jean Arthuis threatening to resign if the government does not make a decision on a new rescue plan for the bank before September 6.
-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe to unveil government's plans to reform income tax over a five-year period this evening at 1800 GMT.
-- Industry Minister Franck Borotra says in an interview says French interests must remain predominant after a merger project between GEC Alsthom ALSF.CN and Framatome.
He said he hopes for a French bidder for auto parts group Valeo this month, and says he favours a car buying incentive scheme.
-- French GDP contracted 0.4 percent in the second quarter, after increasing 1.1 percent in the first quarter.
-- Total posts a 45 percent increase in profit and a 20 percent increase in turnover for the first half.
-- Generale des Eaux seeks to become a telecommunications operator ready to compete with France Telecom when the French telecoms market opens in 1998.
-- Government seeks to tighten health insurance benefits to help control costs.
-- Income tax cuts to be presented by the government today could reach 25 billion francs for 1997, and a total of 75 billion over a five-year period.
-- Italian businessman Carlo De Benedetti steps down as chairman of computer group Olivetti.
-- French authorities remain unenthusiastic over U.S. air strikes against Iraq.
